text:
alex: quick alert  after the kernel-selector change I'm seeing higher host CPU on proxy nodes. p99 tokenize time jumped and grpc small-write syscalls spiked. flame top below. anyone free to triage? :thinking:

kim: which cluster/pool? paste the flame lines and syscall counters. my initial read: serialize-ahead or eager_kernel might be moving work to the host thread and creating many small flushes.

alex: cluster: prod-eu2 proxy pool. flame sample: 
```
  54% host::tokenize::serialize_ahead
  26% net::grpc::small_writev
  12% parse::stream_rechunk
  8% kernel::fallback_variant
```
writev ~= 9-13 calls per 1KB output during spike (lots of 128-256B frames).

jorge: same time window shows kvcache pressure on a few hot shards. evictions spiked ~3x and hit-rate dipped. batching window shrink under load could cause prefixes to flush and slow warmups.

kim: did you try toggling serialize_ahead or changing batch.window_ms? also check the runtime flag stream_coalesce which should aggregate frames before flush.

alex: quick canary toggles: serialize_ahead=enabled + batch.window_ms=5 -> small req CPU -8% but long-seq p99 +4.2%. kvcache hit 0.83 -> 0.70 at peak, evictions/sec 290 -> 1200. writev small reqs 12 -> 3, long reqs 24 -> 34.

jorge: pattern: aggressive serialize reduces syscall count for short flows but hurts long flows because cache warm is delayed and we do more host-side serialization per request. propose test matrix different from usual: 
- 1: serialize_ahead=off, batch.window_ms=5 (baseline)
- 2: serialize_ahead=on, batch.window_ms=5
- 3: serialize_ahead=on, batch.window_ms=20
- 4: serialize_ahead=on, batch.window_ms=20 + batch_coalesce(count=2,max_delay_ms=8) + serialize_offload=true
We should run mixed synthetic: 97% short (6-20 tokens) + 3% long (700-1200 tokens). Measure: p50/p95/p99 host CPU, tokenize wall_ns, syscalls/writev per-request, per-shard kvcache histos, and end-to-end SLO impact.

kim: +1. also instrument serialized_bytes_per_batch and serialize_worker_latency if we offload. collect flame + syscall counters.

alex: infra spun up canary-3 (start 6032109900). /perf run --matrix=3 --trace=flame,kvcache,syscalls posted.

perf-bot: canary-3-6032109900 deploy complete (start 6032109900). health checks: OK.

ops-bot: perf link uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/60321099 (CSV + flame tarball).

jorge: interim results for variant 3: small req CPU -6.3%, long p99 +2.7%, kvcache hit improved to 0.79, evictions/sec down to ~610, writev counts slightly lower overall. serialize wall_ns increased modestly for long sequences.

kim: looks promising for mixed traffic; variant 4 likely to further reduce syscall churn but serialize_offload needs validation: offloading can reduce request-thread work but may add scheduling delays. we must bound offload queue lengths.

alex: action items: 
- kim: run full 1/2/3/4 matrix and post CSVs including per-shard histos and serialize_worker metrics.
- jorge: add microbench that cycles kernel variants and measures serialize_ns, syscall_count_per_kb, and kvcache_lookups per request. add to kernel-selector CI gate.
- alex: file PERF ticket with hypothesis, attach flames/CSVs, and recommend interim flags if matrix 4 is safe: `serialize_ahead=on`, `batch.window_ms=20`, `batch_coalesce(count=2,max_delay_ms=8)`, `serialize_offload=true`, ensure `stream_coalesce=true`. include rollback playbook.

perf-bot: run queued for full matrix. expected completion ~10m.

jorge: one more note  audit flush callsites in streamer/tokenizer. there are a couple of explicit flushes that bypass transport coalescing; moving those to IO thread or deferring by a tick could help.

kim: agreed. if offload looks risky we can instead increase window_ms and tune batch_coalesce as a near-term mitigation.

alex: will keep thread updated. thanks all. :thumbsup:
